definitions.explanation: A bell or electronic device at a door or entrance that visitors press to alert the occupants. Also used for service bells in hotels or restaurants.

examples.japanese: {呼|よ}び{鈴|りん}を{鳴|な}らした。
{呼|よ}び{鈴|りん}が{鳴|な}ったので、{玄関|げんかん}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: The doorbell rang, so I went to the front door.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}も{呼|よ}び{鈴|りん}を{押|お}したが、{誰|だれ}も{出|で}てこなかった。
examples.english: I pressed the doorbell many times, but nobody came out.

notes:
Compound of {呼|よ}び (calling, from {呼|よ}ぶ) and {鈴|りん} (bell). Refers to any bell or button used to summon someone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {呼|よ}び{鈴|りん}を{鳴|な}らす: to ring the doorbell
- {呼|よ}び{鈴|りん}を{押|お}す: to press the doorbell
- {呼|よ}び{鈴|りん}が{鳴|な}る: the doorbell rings

SIMILAR WORDS:
- チャイム: chime — modern electronic doorbell sound; more commonly used in everyday conversation
- インターホン: intercom — doorbell with a speaker/monitor, standard in Japanese apartments
- ベル: bell — general term for bells; also used for doorbells

NOTE:
In modern Japanese, チャイム and インターホン are more commonly used for residential doorbells. {呼|よ}び{鈴|りん} has a slightly old-fashioned nuance but is still widely understood.
